problem:
Your trigger works fine in testing with 5 records. In production, a bulk update of 200 records throws:

System.LimitException:
Too many SOQL queries: 101
explanation: Salesforce allows only 100 SOQL queries per transaction. A query inside a loop multiplies with every record processed. Always query once outside the loop, then use a Map to look up related records per iteration.

problem: Updating a record fires the trigger, which updates the record again, which fires the trigger again — an infinite loop until Salesforce throws a stack depth error.
explanation: A static boolean flag persists for the duration of one transaction. Check it at the start of your handler and set it before doing DML — this stops the trigger from re-entering itself.

problem_title: Null Pointer on a Perfectly Valid Field
problem: acc.Owner.Manager.Email throws a NullPointerException, even though the Account definitely has an Owner.
code:
String email = acc.Owner.Manager.Email;
// NPE if Manager is null anywhere in the chain
fixed_code:
String email = acc?.Owner?.Manager?.Email;
// safe navigation - returns null instead of throwing
explanation: The safe navigation operator (?.) short-circuits the whole expression to null the moment any link in the chain is null, instead of throwing. Available since Apex API v50+.

problem_title: Flow Fails Silently in Production Only
problem: Your Record-Triggered Flow works perfectly in the sandbox. In production, records just don't update — no error banner, nothing in the debug log you can find.
explanation: Check Setup -> Flows -> your flow -> 'View Details and Versions', then look at 'Login History' style Flow error emails sent to the flow's admin. Also verify Save vs Save & Activate — an inactive version silently does nothing while looking identical in the builder.

problem_title: Formula Field Shows Blank Instead of 0
problem: A number formula field that should show '0' shows completely blank whenever one of the source fields is empty.
explanation: In both Formulas and Flow, arithmetic on a null number returns null, not zero — and null displays as blank. Wrap every operand that could be empty in BLANKVALUE() to force it to a real number first.

problem_title: Get Records Returns Nothing, No Error
problem: A Get Records element inside a Flow always returns zero results, even though you can see matching records in the object's list view.
explanation: The most common cause: the Flow runs in 'system context without sharing' or 'user context' and the running user's field-level security or sharing rules quietly filter the record out. Check the flow's run context under Flow properties, and confirm FLS on every filtered field.

problem: Your component's @wire property is undefined on first render, causing a null reference error in your template.
explanation: @wire is asynchronous — the component renders before data arrives. Never assume wired data exists; always guard with optional chaining or a getter, and use template if:true checks in the HTML.

problem_title: Parent-Child Data Update Doesn't Reflect in UI
problem: You mutate an array or object property directly, call the same variable name again, but the template just won't re-render with the new value.
fixed_code:
this.items = [...this.items, newItem];
// new reference triggers reactivity
explanation: LWC's reactivity is based on reference comparison, not deep value comparison. Mutating an array/object in place keeps the same reference, so the framework can't tell anything changed. Always create a new array/object.

problem_title: Aggregate Query Ignores a WHERE Clause
problem: You add a WHERE filter to an aggregate query with GROUP BY, but the totals come back as if the filter wasn't applied at all.
code:
SELECT AccountId, COUNT(Id)
FROM Opportunity
GROUP BY AccountId
HAVING COUNT(Id) > 5
WHERE StageName = 'Closed Won'  -- SYNTAX ERROR
fixed_code:
SELECT AccountId, COUNT(Id)
FROM Opportunity
WHERE StageName = 'Closed Won'
GROUP BY AccountId
HAVING COUNT(Id) > 5
explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping and must come before GROUP BY. HAVING filters the grouped/aggregated results and must come after. Mixing up the order is a very common SOQL mistake.

problem_title: Relationship Query Returns Null for a Field You Know Exists
problem: Account.Owner.Profile.Name comes back null in your query results, even though every user definitely has a profile.
fixed_code:
-- Check FLS/permissions on Profile object access,
-- and confirm the relationship depth (5 levels max
-- for standard, 1 level for custom-to-custom before
-- Spring '21 dot-notation limits)
SELECT Id, Owner.Profile.Name
FROM Account
WHERE Owner.Profile.Name != null
explanation: Traversing relationships in SOQL has depth limits, and the running user's object/field permissions on the parent object silently return null rather than throwing an error. Always check FLS first when a relationship field looks 'missing'.

problem_title: DataRaptor Extract Returns Empty Even Though Data Exists
problem: Your DataRaptor Extract preview shows zero results, but you can see the exact record in Salesforce when you search for it manually.
explanation: Check the Extract's filter values for hardcoded Ids or exact-match strings that don't match your test record's actual data (case-sensitivity matters). Also confirm the running user in preview mode has read access to every field mapped in the output.

problem_title: OmniScript Won't Advance Past a Step
problem: Clicking 'Next' on an OmniScript step does nothing — no error toast, no console error, the user is just stuck.
explanation: This is almost always a required field that's invisible or mis-validated — check for a hidden required Text/Checkbox element with no default value, or a Validation element silently failing. Open browser dev tools and check the Console tab for a swallowed JS error.

problem_title: Integration Procedure Times Out on Large Data Sets
problem: An Integration Procedure that calls a DataRaptor and loops over 500+ records runs fine with test data but times out in production.
explanation: Integration Procedures have a 10-second synchronous limit per transaction chain. For large datasets, use a Batch DataRaptor Transform action, or move heavy record processing into an async Apex Remote Action instead of looping inside the IP itself.

problem_title: Test Class Passes Alone, Fails in Full Run
problem: Your test class passes every time you run it individually, but fails with unexpected data when run as part of the full test suite.
explanation: Tests can see data left behind by other tests unless properly isolated, or can fail due to org-wide data assumptions (like assuming a specific Record Type Id exists). Use @TestSetup and avoid querying real org data — create everything your test needs from scratch.

problem_title: Loop Inside Flow Hits Element Limit
problem: A Flow processing 300 records in a loop throws 'Too many DML statements: 151' — nearly identical to the classic Apex bulkification problem.
code:
// BAD: Update element inside the loop
Loop [Get Records] -> Update Records (each iteration)
fixed_code:
// GOOD: collect into a variable, one Update after the loop
Loop -> Assignment (add to collection)
... after loop ...
Update Records (the whole collection at once)
explanation: Flows have governor limits too. A DML element (Create/Update/Delete Records) inside a loop fires once per record. Collect records into a collection variable during the loop, then perform a single bulk DML operation after it ends.
